newsitem.title: ITALY: Venice's clock tower to be restored.
newsitem.headline: Venice's clock tower to be restored.

text.p: The 15th century clock tower in St Mark's Square in Venice will undergo two years of restoration starting in March, officials said on Friday.
The project is intended to be completed by 1999, when the tower will be 500 years old.

Work on the tower itself will be carried out by the lagoon city's council while the clock's workings will be restored by the Swiss watch manufacturer Piaget. The cost of the work was not immediately disclosed.
The clock tower is the most celebrated of the Italian Renaissance.
The clock's dial is decorated with the signs of the zodiac and two giant bronze Moors strike the hours.
